transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start Time (PST): 16:00
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Tanya (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jen (Redwood CSM), Dara (Acme Sec), Owen (Acme IAM), Priya (Acme Compliance), Samir (Acme Arch)

Summary:
High-level security review focused on SSO (SAML) and provisioning (SCIM) with emphasis on RBAC/least-privilege model appropriate for a regulated healthcare customer. Action items captured for metadata exchange, test tenant provisioning, and RBAC mapping doc. Some minor transcription artifacts below.

[00:00] Tanya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this focused on your SSO/SCIM questions and the RBAC patterns we recommend for healthcare orgs. Marco is our SE who will walk us through details.
[00:22] Marco: Hi all, quick agenda — SAML basics, SCIM provisioning, how we map groups into roles, audit/logging hooks, encryption notes. We'll pause for questions.
[00:37] Dara: Great, thanks. Our priority is least-privilege and making sure provisioning doesn't create over-privileged service accounts. Also need to ensure we meet our internal audit for user lifecycle.
[00:52] Marco: Totally. Two main integration paths: 1) SAML-only SSO with Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning — user created at first login, limited control; 2) SAML + SCIM where SCIM manages user lifecycle and group/attribute syncing. For enterprise you usually want SCIM.
[01:12] Owen: We use Okta primarily, sometimes Azure AD. We want groups to drive RBAC — for example, acme-infra-read, acme-infra-admin, acme-clinical-viewer, etc. How does Redwood map groups to roles?
[01:29] Marco: We support two approaches. Option A: SCIM group-to-role mapping during provisioning — our SCIM endpoint syncs groups, and you configure which group maps to which role in the Console. Option B: SAML assertion map — the SAML assertion contains group attributes, and Redwood consumes them at login to assign transient roles. For long-term provisioning and lifecycle, SCIM is preferred.
[01:52] Priya: For audits we need immutable records of role grants and deprovisioning events. How long are audit logs retained and can they be exported to our SIEM?
[02:08] Marco: Good question — our hosted offering stores audit logs in the Console by default for 90 days. We have a premium retention add-on for 1 year or longer. Logs can stream out via our audit webhook or syslog connector; many customers push to Splunk/Datadog/SIEM. We'll include the endpoint in the follow-up doc.
[02:30] Samir: Are those logs tamper-proof? We need a chain-of-custody for certain actions — admin role changes, role grants, SCIM-provisioned deletions.
[02:45] Marco: Logs are write-once in our internal store and signed; we also emit an append-only event stream that can be mirrored to a customer-owned logging bucket for additional immutability. For the Private deployment we can enable a customer-managed S3 bucket + KMS key to push logs.
[03:02] Dara: Ok. For SAML specifics — NameID formats, assertion consumer URL, certificate rotation — what do you need from us?
[03:12] Tanya: We'll need your IdP metadata XML and confirm the NameID format you prefer (email vs persistent). We recommend email for user-identifiable accounts but if you have an internal persistent identifier we can support that. Also share your preferred signing algorithm; we support RSA-SHA256.
[03:33] Owen: We rotate signing certs quarterly. Does Redwood support multiple active certs during transition windows?
[03:40] Marco: Yes, we accept multiple certs in SP metadata, and our SAML validation allows a rolling window during rotation. We'll include a cert rotation checklist.
[03:54] [04:00] Speaker 1 (Jen): A quick note on SCIM: our SCIM implementation supports bulk group updates and delta sync. We map SCIM group.externalId or displayName to Console roles — there is a mapping UI and API.
[04:14] Owen: Is SCIM provisioning bidirectional? If we change membership in Redwood will it write back?
[04:22] Marco: Not by default. Our SCIM is typically inbound-only (IdP -> Redwood). For two-way provisioning we can evaluate custom integration, but most customers keep SCIM as source of truth in IdP.
[04:36] Priya: For least-privilege, would you recommend many narrowly-scoped roles or a few broad roles?
[04:45] Marco: We recommend role granularity aligned with job function and approval boundaries — e.g., Viewer, Operator (limited writes), Admin. For healthcare, separate roles for data access vs infra operations is common. We'll share patterns and a sample mapping for Acme.
[04:58] Dara: Can we make temporary elevated roles for a time window (just-in-time elevation)?
[05:06] Marco: We support ephemeral elevation via our Console with audit and expiration. You can trigger an elevation for a user for X hours, recorded in the audit log and optionally require approval.
[05:20] Owen: On SCIM group attribute mapping — can we map nested groups or groups-of-groups? Our Okta uses nested groups for org structure.
[05:30] Marco: Our SCIM sync flattens nested groups by default but we can configure hierarchical mapping in the POC. We'll note caveats where nested memberships increase provisioning churn.
[05:46] Priya: Encryption questions: do you encrypt keys at rest, and can we use our own KMS?
[05:55] Marco: Data at rest is encrypted. For hosted customers we use a Redwood-managed KMS by default but support customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private. You can provide a KMS key (AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault) for encryption of customer blobs and keys. We'll attach the KMS whitepaper in the follow-up.
[06:20] Tanya: Quick call-out — for healthcare PII/PHI workflows we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments for increased control over keys and network isolation. Dara, is your current procurement leaning toward hosted or private?
[06:34] Dara: For the pilot we'd like hosted in a data residency region (US-East) but eventually Dedicated or Private is on the table if we move to production.
[06:48] Marco: Understood. We'll show a path: start with hosted in region with CMK option later when you commit to Dedicated.
[07:00] Owen: Back to SAML — attribute mapping: we want email, employeeId, title, and a custom claim for license_level. How do you surface custom claims?
[07:11] Marco: SAML attribute mapping can map arbitrary attributes into user profile fields. For license_level we map to a user.profile.custom_license which can be evaluated in our policy engine to gate features.
[07:26] Jen: (slight crosstalk) Also note that our API tokens respect RBAC so token-scoped permissions are limited. You can create machine roles and token policies.
[07:38] Samir: Can we enforce SSO-only login? I.e., disable password auth entirely.
[07:45] Marco: Yes, you can enforce SSO-only at org or team level. Password login can be disabled and will be blocked for all non-SSO accounts.
[08:00] Dara: What about SCIM deprovisioning? If a user is removed in Okta, how quickly is access revoked? We need near real-time for HIPAA concerns.
[08:10] Marco: SCIM deprovisioning is typically processed within seconds-to-minutes; depends on the idp->Redwood sync cadence. With push-based provisioning from Okta it's near-instant. We'll confirm timing in the POC.
[08:26] Owen: For service accounts and machines — we prefer machine-to-machine auth via client certs or mTLS rather than SCIM. Does Redwood support mTLS for internal services?
[08:38] Marco: We provide token-based service accounts and support mutual TLS for Private deployments. For hosted we issue short-lived service tokens with granular scopes; for Dedicated/Private you can enable mTLS.
[08:52] Priya: Auditability — we need to show: who granted role X, when, justification. Can you capture justification during elevation?
[09:00] Marco: Yes; the elevation flow can require a reason field and approver. All are stored in the audit record and exportable.
[09:12] [09:30] Speaker 2 (Dara): There's noise on our side. Sorry.
[09:38] Dara: Regarding SCIM user attributes, we want to sync employeeType and location attributes for access controls — can Redwood use those attributes for ABAC-style policies?
[09:52] Marco: Our policy engine supports attribute-based checks on profile fields — you can write a rule like allow if user.profile.employeeType == 'full_time' and user.profile.location == 'US-East'. We'll include examples.
[10:08] Owen: For RBAC, we need an emergency break-glass admin who bypasses SSO in total emergency. Is that possible and how is it controlled?
[10:18] Marco: We provision a break-glass admin with offline keys and strict controls; access is logged heavily and triggers an alert. Break-glass usage can be limited to specific IP ranges and require multi-party approval.
[10:32] Priya: On compliance artifacts — can you provide SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 cert, and penetration test summaries?
[10:41] Tanya: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 attestation and ISO summary. Pen test redacted reports are available under NDA; we'll add this to next steps.
[10:55] Samir: On the RBAC UI — can we programmatically manage role mappings via API for automation?
[11:03] Marco: Absolutely. Role creation, assignment, and mapping APIs exist and are documented. Many infra teams automate role sync in their CI/CD. We'll send examples.
[11:16] Dara: Can the SCIM integration create service principals (non-human identities) and assign only machine roles?
[11:24] Marco: SCIM is scoped to users and groups; for service principals we recommend service tokens or SAML-backed machine certs. You can still assign a group that contains machine identities via your IdP.
[11:38] Jen: A couple of practical items — sample SAML metadata, SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated flows, ACS URL, and expected saml:audience — we'll attach sample configs in the doc.
[11:54] Owen: About SCIM rate limits — during a big org sync, what throttling exists? We have 10k users and large groups.
[12:04] Marco: Our SCIM endpoint supports bulk endpoints and has configurable throttle for Enterprise. For initial onboarding we can bump quotas for your org during the POC to avoid failures.
[12:18] Priya: For the RBAC model review, can we get a sample least-privilege role list for healthcare customers?
[12:26] Marco: Yes — sample will include roles like ClinicalViewer, ClinicalEditor (no infra), InfraOperator (deploy pipelines), BillingViewer, Admin. We'll annotate each with allowed API scopes.
[12:40] [12:52] Dara: Are there delegations, e.g., allow team leads to grant Viewer in their team only?
[12:58] Marco: We support scoped admins — you can scope role admin permission to certain org units or teams. This is in the Console and programmable via API.
[13:12] Owen: For attestations, can we do periodic access reviews and export attestations to our GRC tool?
[13:20] Marco: Yes, we have an Access Review API and periodic reports exportable as CSV/JSON. Many customers integrate with OneTrust/Workday for attestations.
[13:34] Priya: Will the POC include a test where we deprovision a user and validate data access is removed?
[13:42] Marco: Yes, we typically do that as part of the POC checklist — we'll run a create/login/provision, modify groups, and deprovision cycle.
[13:54] Samir: If we later want Private deployment, are the SSO/SCIM flows identical? Any differences?
[14:03] Marco: The protocols are the same; Private gives you more control over network and KMS. For Private you manage the Certs and KMS, and audits are stored in your environment.
[14:18] Dara: One more question on data residency — if a user with EU residency logs in, where is profile data stored?
[14:28] Marco: For hosted we pin orgs to regions; profile metadata and logs are stored in the region chosen. For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private to keep everything in your VPC.
[14:42] Owen: Do you support SCIM over mutual TLS?
[14:48] Marco: Yes, SCIM can be configured over mTLS for additional security for inbound provisioning endpoints.
[15:00] Priya: Concerning lifecycle, we need preservation of historical role assignments for compliance 7-year retention. Is that feasible?
[15:10] Marco: Our default retention isn't that long; however, with log export to your S3 and lifecycle policies you can retain for 7+ years. We'll include the export workflow in the docs.
[15:26] Tanya: Quick recap — we will: send SAML metadata, sample attribute mappings, SCIM endpoints and API keys for test Okta tenant, RBAC mapping doc, and SOC 2/ISO artifacts. Acme will provide test Okta admin, confirm region, and share initial role list.
[15:46] Dara: Sounds good. Also please include the cert rotation checklist and example SAML assertion (with redacted values).
[15:56] Marco: Will do.
[16:02] [16:20] (some cross talk; background noise)
[16:30] Owen: One smaller thing — do you have built-in SAML metadata signing? We sign IdP metadata but want to be sure SP metadata is also signed.
[16:38] Marco: Yes, SP metadata can include signature and we'll export signed metadata for your IdP.
[16:46] Priya: Anything else on encryption keys? If we use customer-managed KMS, what granularity do keys have? Per-org, per-team?
[16:58] Marco: We support per-org CMKs and can support per-tenant/per-environment keys for Dedicated/Private. We'll outline recommended approaches and cost tradeoffs.
[17:12] Tanya: Great. We'll follow up with the docs and set the POC timeline.
[17:20] Dara: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[17:28] Marco: Thanks — we'll get the RBAC template to you today.
[17:36] Jen: I'll set the follow-up meeting for the week of Feb 24 and invite the IAM engineer.
[17:46] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-attribution and ambient noise; some sentences may be truncated by the auto-transcription. Links referenced: https://docs.redwood.com/sso-guide (sample), https://redwood.com/security/soc2 (redacted link).
